# Rates Prototype
```{r}
assign_tariffs_to_month_hour_grid <- function(month_hour_grid, tariffs) {
  # Process each tariff and create a lookup table
  lookup_table <- tariffs %>%

    # Must operate rowwise()
    rowwise() %>%

    # create 2 lists:
    #     months for all the months covered, including handling wraparound
    #     hours for all the hours covered, again including handling wraparound
    mutate(
      # Create a list of months covered by this tariff_season_period combination
      months = list(if (start_month <= end_month) {
        start_month:end_month
      } else {
        c(start_month:12, 1:end_month)
      }),
      # Create a list of hours covered by this tariff
      hours = list(if (start_hour <= end_hour) {
        start_hour:end_hour
      } else {
        c(start_hour:23, 0:end_hour)
      })
    ) |>

    # Now create a table that we can join with the month_hour_grid
    # Expand the months and hours
    unnest(months) |>
    unnest(hours) |>

    # Select only the columns we need
    select(month = months, hour = hours, value)


  # Before joining, check for duplicate month-hour combinations in the lookup table
  duplicate_check <- lookup_table %>%
    group_by(month, hour) %>%
    summarize(
      count = n(),
      values = paste(unique(value), collapse = ", "),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(count > 1)

  if (nrow(duplicate_check) > 0) {
    warning("Found duplicate values for some month-hour combinations:")
    print(duplicate_check)

    # We'll use the first value for each month-hour combination
    lookup_table <- lookup_table %>%
      group_by(month, hour) %>%
      slice(1) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  month_hour_tariff <- month_hour_grid %>%
    left_join(lookup_table, by = c("month", "hour"))

  # Check for missing values
  missing_count <- sum(is.na(month_hour_tariff$value))
  if (missing_count > 0) {
    warning(paste("There are", missing_count, "month-hour combinations without a value"))
  }

  return(month_hour_tariff)
}


```

```{r}
# this one works
library(tidyverse)

bldg_ids = c(217291, 448378, 309696, 102137, 409444, 107049, 490878, 249001, 46306, 405471)

# Read from the database
path_rs_db <-"/workspaces/reports/data/ResStock/2022_resstock_amy2018_release_1.1/rs_20250307.db"
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), path_rs_db)

# Hourly
hourly_load_2022_raw <- tbl(con, "NY_hourly") |>
  filter(upgrade == 4) |>
  filter(bldg_id %in% bldg_ids) |>
  select(
    bldg_id,
    upgrade,
    month,
    day,
    hour,
    elec_consumption = `sum_out.electricity.total.energy_consumption`
  ) |>
  collect()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# Temporary: randomly assign bldgs to utilities
# First create mapping of building IDs to utilities
bldg_utility_map <- tibble(
  bldg_id = unique(hourly_load_2022_raw$bldg_id),
  utility = sample(c("national_grid", "eversource_nstar", "eversource_wme_co", "unitil"),
                  size = length(unique(hourly_load_2022_raw$bldg_id)),
                  replace = TRUE)
)

# Then join this mapping to the monthly load data
hourly_load_2022 <- hourly_load_2022_raw |>
  left_join(bldg_utility_map, by = "bldg_id")

# Monthly
monthly_load_2022_raw <- hourly_load_2022 |>
  filter(upgrade == 4) |>
  select(
    bldg_id,
    upgrade,
    month,
    elec_consumption
  ) |>
  filter(bldg_id %in% bldg_ids) |>
  summarize (
    .by = c(bldg_id, upgrade, month),
    elec_consumption = sum(elec_consumption)
  )
```

```{r}

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), path_rs_db)

# the duckDB at con has a table called "NY_hourly" that has the hourly load data
# that's 8760 hours x 33676 bldg_ids = 295M rows...much more than we can fit into memory
# we need to add the month_hour_tariff table to the db as a temporary table, then join it with NY_hourly INSIDE the db

# Add month_hour_tariff to the db
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "month_hour_tariff", month_hour_tariff, overwrite = TRUE)

# Join month_hour_tariff with NY_hourly inside the db
query <- sprintf("
SELECT
    nyh.bldg_id,
    nyh.upgrade,
    nyh.month,
    SUM(nyh.\"sum_out.electricity.total.energy_consumption\") AS monthly_consumption,
    SUM(nyh.\"sum_out.electricity.total.energy_consumption\" * mht.value) AS monthly_delivery_charge
FROM
    NY_hourly AS nyh
LEFT JOIN
    month_hour_tariff AS mht
ON
    nyh.month = mht.month AND
    nyh.hour = mht.hour
WHERE
    nyh.bldg_id IN (%s)
GROUP BY
    nyh.bldg_id,
    nyh.upgrade,
    nyh.month
ORDER BY
    nyh.bldg_id,
    nyh.month
", paste(bldg_ids, collapse = ","))

monthly_load_with_tariffs <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, query)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

```


# Calculate Bills
## Monthly Bills
```{r}

calculate_monthly_bills <- function(monthly_load, tariffs, supply_rates) {
  monthly_load |>

    # Part 1: Tariffs -> 3 joins for customer_charge, delivery_rate, sales_tax
    left_join(
      tariffs |>
        filter(type == "customer_charge") |>
        select(month, utility, value, version, tariff_id) |>
        rename(customer_charge = value),
        by = c(month, utility)
    ) |>
    left_join(
      tariffs |>
        filter(type == "delivery_rate") |>
        select(month, utility, value, version, tariff_id) |>
        rename(delivery_rate = value),
        by = c(month, utility)
    ) |>
    left_join(
      tariffs |>
        filter(type == "sales_tax_rate") |>
        select(month, utility, value, version, tariff_id) |>
        rename(sales_tax_rate = value),
        by = c(month, utility)
    ) |>

    # Part 2: Supply rates -> join on utility and month
    left_join(
      supply_rates,
      by = c("month", "utility")
    ) |>

    # Part 3: Calculate monthly bill
    mutate(
      delivery_charge = elec_consumption * delivery_rate,
      supply_charge = elec_consumption * supply_rate,
      total_pretax_bill = supply_charge + delivery_charge + customer_charge,
      sales_tax_charge = total_pretax_bill * sales_tax_rate,
      total_bill = total_pretax_bill + sales_tax_charge
    ) |>
    arrange(bldg_id, month, upgrade, version, tariff_id)
}

monthly_bills_2022 <- calculate_monthly_bills(monthly_load_2022,
                                            tariffs,
                                            supply_rates_monthly_ma_2024)

```

## Annual Bills
```{r}

calculate_annual_bills_from_monthly <- function(monthly_bills) {
  monthly_bills |>
    group_by(bldg_id, upgrade, version, tariff_id) |>
    summarize(
      annual_bill = sum(total_bill)
    ) |>
    collect()
}

annual_bills_2022 <- calculate_annual_bills_from_monthly(monthly_bills_2022)

```

# Plots (for sanity checking)
```{r}
library(patchwork)  # Add this at the top with other library imports

# Get the overall x-axis limits from all data
min_bill <- 0
max_bill <- 25000

p1 <- annual_bills_2022 |>
  filter(version == "hpr_doer") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = annual_bill)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#68BED8", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "HPR DOER", x = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    limits = c(min_bill, max_bill)
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p2 <- annual_bills_2022 |>
  filter(version == "hpr_approved") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = annual_bill)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#FC9706", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "HPR Approved", x = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    limits = c(min_bill, max_bill)
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p3 <- annual_bills_2022 |>
  filter(version == "baseline") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = annual_bill)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#023047", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Baseline", x = "Annual Bill ($)") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    limits = c(min_bill, max_bill)
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Combine plots vertically using patchwork
p1 / p2 / p3 +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
  )
```
